title: Haldi relief read as a spearhead; sites called fortresses (kalesi)

tellings.quote: warlike they believe archaeologists believe firmly that what they're passing in their hand is a spearhead

plain: Near Lake Van in eastern Turkey there is an ancient carving known as the Haldi relief, and archaeologists read the object one figure passes in its hand as a spearhead. A researcher named Matt LaCroix describes this reading without naming a source, saying archaeologists "believe firmly" it is a weapon and so see the people as warlike. He adds that the old sites there are called fortresses, "kalesi" in Turkish, and he presents both readings as the experts' view, implying the carvings may mean something else.
